articles.title: Singapore launches matchmaking service for government workers
articles.summary: The launch of FirstDate comes as the ageing nation wrestles with a record-low fertility rate.
articles.content:
Singapore has rolled out a matchmaking service for its government workers, an initiative that comes as the country wrestles with a record-low fertility rate.

FirstDate, which launched this week for those aged 21 to 35, boasts "a different approach to dating", where it uses a Nobel-winning algorithm to match participants to one date at a time. "Swipe fatigue ends here," its website reads.

Participants sign in using the national digital identity system and answer a survey about their interests, habits and values.

FirstDate's launch drew mixed responses among Singaporeans, with some describing it as "dystopian" and others saying they would be keen to give it a shot.

On its website, FirstDate highlights the Gale-Shapley Stable Marriage algorithm which powers the programme.

The mathematical framework pairs two equally sized groups of people based on their preferences.

The late mathematician Lloyd Shapley was awarded the 2012 Nobel memorial prize in economic sciences for discovering the algorithm, which has been used in public school admissions, medical residency matching, and dating apps, among other things.

"At the end of the day, I think the experience of meeting someone through an application doesn't change much across the [different types of] applications," Elizabeth, a 29-year-old who works in Singapore's defence ministry and is keen on trying FirstDate out told the BBC.

"But it is nice to know that the likelihood of being scammed is much lower. We're all public servants looking for a partner, right?"

But some social media users say the initiative, which is currently in its pilot phase, discriminates against those not working in government.

Others criticised the age limit. "They are only doing this to raise the total fertility rate. They don't actually [care] about whether we find a partner otherwise.

"Since there are higher risks involved in having kids at 35 and older, the government just writes [the older singles] off," wrote another Reddit user.

It is not clear if the pilot programme will be available to the wider public in future. The BBC has reached out to GovTech, the statutory board behind the pilot, for comment.

The pilot launch comes as Singapore's birth rate has slumped to historic lows. For the first time in the past 60 years, fewer than 30,000 babies were born in 2025.

The number of deaths meanwhile have been rising steadily in the greying nation, hitting about 26,500 in 2025.

In August, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced a series of new measures to better support families and to encourage couples to have children, including almost S$70,000 ($54,000; £41,000) in financial support for every child by the time they turn 17.
articles.reasoning: The article reports on Singapore's government launching a matchmaking service for public servants to address the country's record-low fertility rate, which is a significant social challenge. The initiative uses a Nobel-winning algorithm to improve dating outcomes, potentially helping individuals find partners and encouraging family formation. This has broad societal implications for demographic sustainability and family support policies, making it an inspiring and hopeful social innovation with tangible benefits for the population.
articles.personality_title: Singapore launches matchmaking service for government workers to boost family growth
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Singapore is facing a record-low birth rate, with fewer babies born than ever before in 60 years. The country wants to encourage more couples to start families and support them financially.

**What happened** – This week, Singapore introduced FirstDate, a matchmaking service specifically for government workers aged 21 to 35. It uses a special Nobel Prize-winning algorithm called the Gale-Shapley Stable Marriage algorithm to match people based on their interests and preferences. Participants sign in using their national ID and answer questions about their habits and values.

**Impact** – FirstDate aims to make dating easier and safer for public servants by reducing the chance of scams and focusing on meaningful matches. This is important because it supports family formation in a country where the number of births is very low, and the population is getting older. The program could help more people find partners and eventually have children.

**What's next step** – Right now, FirstDate is only a pilot program for government workers. It is not yet known if it will be available to everyone in Singapore. Officials are watching how well it works and may decide to expand it or create similar services.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Singapore’s new matchmaking service uses smart technology to help government workers find partners and address the country’s low birth rate.
articles.personality_title_fr: Singapour lance un service de rencontres pour les fonctionnaires afin de favoriser la croissance des familles
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Singapour fait face à un taux de natalité historiquement bas, avec moins de naissances qu’au cours des 60 dernières années. Le pays souhaite encourager les couples à fonder une famille et leur apporter un soutien financier.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Cette semaine, Singapour a lancé FirstDate, un service de rencontres destiné aux fonctionnaires âgés de 21 à 35 ans. Il utilise un algorithme primé au Nobel, appelé l’algorithme du mariage stable de Gale-Shapley, pour associer les personnes selon leurs intérêts et préférences. Les participants se connectent avec leur identité numérique nationale et répondent à un questionnaire sur leurs habitudes et valeurs.

**Impact** – FirstDate vise à faciliter et sécuriser les rencontres pour les fonctionnaires en réduisant les risques d’arnaques et en favorisant des correspondances significatives. Cela est important pour soutenir la formation des familles dans un pays où le nombre de naissances est très faible et la population vieillit. Ce programme peut aider davantage de personnes à trouver un partenaire et à avoir des enfants.

**Prochaines étapes** – Pour l’instant, FirstDate est un programme pilote réservé aux fonctionnaires. On ne sait pas encore s’il sera ouvert à toute la population de Singapour. Les autorités observent ses résultats et pourraient décider de l’étendre ou de créer des services similaires.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Le nouveau service de rencontres de Singapour utilise une technologie intelligente pour aider les fonctionnaires à trouver un partenaire et à répondre au faible taux de natalité du pays.
articles.personality_title_es: Singapur lanza un servicio de citas para empleados públicos para fomentar el crecimiento familiar
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Singapur enfrenta una tasa de natalidad históricamente baja, con menos bebés nacidos que en los últimos 60 años. El país quiere animar a las parejas a formar familias y brindarles apoyo financiero.

**Qué pasó** – Esta semana, Singapur lanzó FirstDate, un servicio de citas dirigido a empleados públicos de entre 21 y 35 años. Utiliza un algoritmo ganador del Premio Nobel llamado algoritmo de matrimonio estable de Gale-Shapley para emparejar personas según sus intereses y preferencias. Los participantes inician sesión con su identidad digital nacional y responden preguntas sobre sus hábitos y valores.

**Impacto** – FirstDate busca facilitar y hacer más seguro el proceso de citas para los empleados públicos, reduciendo el riesgo de fraudes y enfocándose en emparejamientos significativos. Esto es importante para apoyar la formación de familias en un país donde la natalidad es muy baja y la población envejece. El programa podría ayudar a más personas a encontrar pareja y tener hijos.

**Próximo paso** – Actualmente, FirstDate es un programa piloto solo para empleados públicos. No se sabe si se abrirá al público en general en Singapur. Las autoridades están observando su funcionamiento y podrían decidir expandirlo o crear servicios similares.

**Resumen en una frase** – El nuevo servicio de citas de Singapur usa tecnología inteligente para ayudar a empleados públicos a encontrar pareja y enfrentar la baja tasa de natalidad del país.

articles.title: People troll my DIY but they just spur me on
articles.summary: Female DIY experts and tradeswomen talk about their experiences of a traditionally male-dominated domain.
articles.content:
It's hard to miss the explosion of DIY content that has hit our social media feeds over the last decade.

From quick reels on how to fix cracks in walls, to complicated YouTube tutorials on building alcove seating from scratch, the internet is chock-a-block with seemingly endless home improvement demos.

While DIY was once seen as more of a male domain, female influencers are inspiring a new generation of women to take matters into their own hands.

Meanwhile, demand for female professionals is rising, while some women are changing careers to take up trades which they see as more AI-proof than their desk jobs.
articles.reasoning: The article highlights women breaking gender barriers in the traditionally male-dominated DIY and trades sector, inspiring others and promoting gender equality and empowerment in the workforce. It addresses a meaningful social change with broad relevance.
articles.personality_title: Women reshape DIY and trades with new skills and confidence
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – DIY, or 'do it yourself,' has long been seen as a job mostly for men. But in recent years, many women have started sharing their own home repair and building projects online.

**What happened** – Female DIY experts and tradeswomen are using social media to teach people how to fix and build things. They post videos and tutorials that show step-by-step guides, from simple repairs to complex projects. Some women are even switching careers to become professional tradesworkers because they believe these jobs are more secure and less likely to be replaced by computers.

**Impact** – This change is important because it challenges old ideas about what jobs women and men should do. Seeing women succeed in DIY and trades encourages more girls and women to try these skills. It also helps create more equal job opportunities and brings fresh talent to fields that have been mostly male.

**What's next step** – As more women join the trades and share their work online, the community will grow. This could lead to more support, training, and jobs for women in these areas. It might also inspire schools and companies to encourage girls to learn hands-on skills early.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Women are breaking into DIY and trades, inspiring others and helping change who builds and fixes things in our world.
articles.personality_title_fr: Des femmes transforment le bricolage et les métiers avec de nouvelles compétences et confiance
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Le bricolage, ou « faire soi-même », a longtemps été considéré comme un domaine surtout masculin. Mais ces dernières années, de nombreuses femmes ont commencé à partager leurs propres projets de réparation et de construction sur internet.

**Ce qui s'est passé** – Des expertes en bricolage et des femmes artisanes utilisent les réseaux sociaux pour montrer comment réparer et construire. Elles publient des vidéos et des tutoriels qui expliquent pas à pas, des réparations simples aux projets complexes. Certaines changent même de carrière pour devenir professionnelles du bâtiment, car elles pensent que ces métiers sont plus sûrs et moins menacés par les ordinateurs.

**Impact** – Ce changement est important car il remet en cause les idées anciennes sur les métiers des hommes et des femmes. Voir des femmes réussir dans le bricolage et les métiers attire plus de filles et de femmes à apprendre ces compétences. Cela aide aussi à créer plus d’égalité dans l’emploi et apporte de nouveaux talents dans des secteurs longtemps masculins.

**Prochaine étape** – À mesure que de plus en plus de femmes rejoignent les métiers et partagent leur travail en ligne, la communauté grandira. Cela pourrait conduire à plus de soutien, de formations et d’emplois pour les femmes. Cela pourrait aussi encourager les écoles et les entreprises à initier tôt les filles aux compétences pratiques.

**Une phrase clé** – Les femmes s’imposent dans le bricolage et les métiers, inspirant les autres et changeant qui construit et répare dans notre monde.
articles.personality_title_es: Las mujeres transforman el bricolaje y oficios con nuevas habilidades y confianza
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – El bricolaje, o 'hazlo tú mismo', durante mucho tiempo se ha visto como una tarea principalmente para hombres. Pero en los últimos años, muchas mujeres han empezado a compartir sus propios proyectos de reparación y construcción en internet.

**Qué pasó** – Expertas en bricolaje y mujeres trabajadoras del oficio usan las redes sociales para enseñar cómo reparar y construir cosas. Publican videos y tutoriales con instrucciones paso a paso, desde arreglos simples hasta proyectos complejos. Algunas mujeres incluso cambian de carrera para ser profesionales del oficio porque creen que estos trabajos son más seguros y menos reemplazables por computadoras.

**Impacto** – Este cambio es importante porque desafía ideas antiguas sobre qué trabajos deben hacer hombres y mujeres. Ver a mujeres tener éxito en el bricolaje y los oficios anima a más niñas y mujeres a aprender estas habilidades. También ayuda a crear oportunidades laborales más iguales y trae nuevos talentos a campos que antes eran mayormente masculinos.

**Próximo paso** – A medida que más mujeres se unan a los oficios y compartan su trabajo en línea, la comunidad crecerá. Esto podría llevar a más apoyo, formación y empleos para mujeres. También podría inspirar a escuelas y empresas a animar a las niñas a aprender habilidades prácticas desde temprano.

**Una frase clave** – Las mujeres irrumpen en el bricolaje y los oficios, inspirando a otros y cambiando quién construye y arregla cosas en nuestro mundo.
